messages:
elaine: heads-up — we found a GCP service account key in a partner webhook payload that hit our ingest logs around 2024-07-12 14:03 UTC. not in cleartext on S3 but captured in app logs before redaction. tagging cleanup/rotation here.

samir: yikes. which SA? can you paste the last 8 chars (no full key)?

elaine: svc-prod-ingest@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com — last 8 of key id: a1b2c3d4. sample log line (redacted):
```
INFO Received webhook from partner-x, headers: {...}, body: {"payload": "...","service_key":"REDACTED***a1b2c3d4"}
```

jordan: immediate checklist: 1) revoke the key 2) create new key 3) update partner integration 4) rotate any cached creds (k8s secret / vault) 5) audit logs for lateral use. agree?

elaine: yep. I'm about to run a scoped revoke. will also open a vault rotation ticket for anything referencing that SA.

security-bot: automated alert: token-usage spike detected for svc-prod-ingest between 2024-07-12T14:00Z and 2024-07-12T14:15Z — 87 calls from two external IPs. logged to #incidents and created INCIDENT-20240712-15.

oncall-sre: if there's an active incident, please freeze deploys for services that can trigger partner callbacks for 30m. I can set a firewall rule to block the two IPs if needed.

samir: hold off on blocking until we confirm partner involvement. if partner sent the key in their payload, likely not an attacker using the key yet, but could be exfil from their infra. we should:
- revoke key immediately (low blast radius since ingest SA only used by partner integration)
- create a new key and rotate consumers
- rotate any Kubernetes secrets and Vault entries that reference this key id
- enable IAM condition: restrict key usage to caller IP ranges and runtime identity where possible

elaine: revoking now: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable a1b2c3d4 --iam-account=svc-prod-ingest@...` then `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete a1b2c3d4 --iam-account=...` — will post back with output.

elaine: deleted. `gcloud` returned 200 for delete. created new key and uploaded to a temp vault path: `vault kv put secret/rotations/svc-prod-ingest key_json=@newkey.json metadata=rot-20240712` — filing rotation ticket to update k8s sealed secret and partner.

maria: for partner coordination: draft message saying we revoked one key because it appeared in logs and ask them to confirm how it was included. we should share a minimal time window, the key id suffix, and recommended mitigation on their side (avoid logging secrets, replace stored keys with environment-only). happy to draft.

jordan: also audit KMS/Vault usage: check if any tokens were unwrapped by the key prior to revoke. query our vault-audit logs: `gcloud logging read \"resource.type=service_account AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\\\"svc-prod-ingest@...\\\" AND timestamp>=\\\"2024-07-12T13:50:00Z\\\"\"` and `vault audit list` entries for the same window.

elaine: running the queries now. quick grep shows no downstream calls using that key id after 14:05 UTC. will post full audit snippet once done.

security-bot: note: ECS task role bindings referencing that SA in metadata were found in one staging cluster config map — flagged to ops-config for rewrite.

samir: follow-up items and owners:
- elaine: partner notification + revoke log + ticket link (INC-20240712-15)
- jordan: run full vault/gcloud audit and attach findings
- maria: draft partner outreach (cc legal if they confirm leak)
- oncall-sre: temporary firewall block if partner confirms active abuse
- samir/security: review RBAC: consider adding IAM Conditions to limit key use and add org-level logging retention for 90d

elaine: created PR to rotate sealed secret: `infra/ops#482` — will merge after partner confirms new key reception.

maria: partner outreach draft ready, PTAL: "We rotated a service key that appeared in request payloads. Please confirm any internal incidents and stop logging secrets in payloads. We recommend issuing a new key on your side and switching to a signed HMAC-based handshake or OAuth flow."

jordan: suggestion: move partner integration to a token exchange pattern: partner presents a short-lived signed assertion and we mint a short-lived token (1h) for ingestion — avoids long-lived keys in payloads. Add to backlog for Q3 work.

elaine: audit results attached to ticket: no evidence of exfil beyond partner payloads. closing immediate rotation task; keeping incident open for partner confirmation and postmortem.

samir: good. add an item: run a repo search for accidental logging patterns `service_key|private_key|secret` across partner SDKs and our middleware. will have devex run that scan.

oncall-sre: I've held off firewall blocks. if partner confirms no malicious use, we can reopen normal traffic. otherwise I'll block and escalate.

maria: legal asked for the partner's POP timeline if they confirm internal exposure; I've queued a DM to legal with incident summary.

elaine: thanks all — closing the rotation subtask, leaving incident open for partner confirmation and RBAC follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
